amos.1.p1.b1.text: These are the words of Amos, who was among the sheepherders of Tekoa—what he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake, in the days when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel.

amos.1.p1.b2.text: He said: “The LORD roars from Zion and raises His voice from Jerusalem;

amos.1.p1.b3.text: the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers.”

amos.1.p1.b4.text: This is what the LORD says: “For three transgressions of Damascus, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they threshed Gilead with sledges of iron.

amos.1.p1.b5.text: So I will send fire upon the house of Hazael to consume the citadels of Ben-hadad.

amos.1.p1.b6.text: I will break down the gates of Damascus; … The people of Aram will be exiled to Kir,” says the LORD.

amos.1.p2.b1.text: “For three transgressions of Gaza, even four, I will not revoke My judgment, because they exiled a whole population, delivering them up to Edom.

amos.1.p2.b2.text: “For three transgressions of Tyre, even four, … because they delivered up a whole congregation of exiles to Edom and broke a covenant of brotherhood.

amos.1.p2.b3.text: “For three transgressions of Edom, even four, … because he pursued his brother with the sword and stifled all compassion; his anger raged continually, and his fury flamed incessantly.

amos.1.p2.b4.text: “For three transgressions of the Ammonites, even four, … in order to enlarge their territory.

amos.1.p2.b5.text: So I will kindle a fire in the walls of Rabbah to consume its citadels amid war cries on the day of battle and a violent wind on the day of tempest.

amos.1.p2.b6.text: Their king will go into exile — he and his princes together,” says the LORD.
